ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that there is a line $AE$, and $O$ is a point on line $AE$. $OB$ is the bisector of $\angle AOC$, $OD$ is the bisector of $\angle COE$. If $\angle AOB=30^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle COE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since OB is the bisector of $\angle AOC$ and $\angle AOB=30^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BOC=\angle AOB=30^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle AOC=2\angle AOB=60^\circ$.\\
Since $\angle AOC+\angle COE=180^\circ$,\\
we have $\angle COE=180^\circ-\angle AOC=180^\circ-60^\circ=\boxed{120^\circ}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Since $OB$ is the bisector of $\angle AOC$ and $\angle AOB=30^\circ$, we have $\angle BOC=30^\circ$, so $\angle AOC=60^\circ$. Since $\angle AOC+\angle COE=180^\circ$, it follows that $\angle COE=180^\circ-60^\circ=\boxed{120^\circ}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, AE is a horizontal straight line passing through point O, E is on the left side of O, and A is on the right side of O; starting from O there are three upward rays, among which OB goes toward the upper right, OC is higher than OB, and OD goes toward the upper left. The problem gives that OB is the angle bisector of ∠AOC, and OD is the angle bisector of ∠COE. Reasoning: Because OB bisects ∠AOC, ∠AOB = ∠BOC. It is known that ∠AOB = 30°, therefore ∠BOC = 30°, and thus ∠AOC = 30° + 30° = 60°. Also because OA and OE are opposite rays on the same straight line, ∠AOC and ∠COE form a straight angle, and their sum is 180°. Therefore ∠COE = 180° - 60° = 120°.
